title: Lockless Snapshot Resume: resumable, low-latency VPC data-plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an upgrade operator and IaC hooks that allow stateful data-plane/runtime rollouts in customer VPCs with zero-downtime and resumable rollback while minimizing locking and tenant blast radius.

Problem statement: Current upgrade flows rely on heavy global coordination and opaque draining which causes long tail downtime for some tenants and brittle rollbacks in the event of partial failure. For private (VPC) deployments we need a mechanism that: (1) avoids cluster-wide locks, (2) supports interrupted upgrades with resume semantics, (3) keeps KV caches warm to maintain low P50/P95 latency, and (4) enables deterministic rollback that restores live traffic quickly.

Design overview: "Lockless Snapshot Resume" operator. High-level steps: (1) Each node performs consistent incremental snapshots of in-memory KV/cache and ephemeral session metadata into the customer's object store (S3/GCS) using a versioned prefix; snapshots are chunked and checksummed to allow partial resume. (2) The control-plane sequencer (operator) coordinates per-tenant checkpoint fencing using lease tokens but does not acquire a global lock; leases are granular by slice/tenant. (3) During upgrade, new node instances are created with a staged bootstrap flow: download latest snapshot shards, apply local replay to restore KV & session caches, start in read-only warm phase, run synthetic probe traffic for priming, then flip to active with a traffic fence enforcement that routes a small shadow percentage and gradually ramps. (4) Rollback path reuses the snapshots: if a target release is unhealthy, operator spins up last-known-good nodes, replays snapshot shards, and performs canary routing until health gates pass.

Health gates and observability: Multi-axis gating: service health (tail latency P99 < threshold), correctness (synthetic prompt consistency via token-diff metric), cache-warmth (KV hit rate > X%), and infra health (GPU utilization under cap). For correctness we run deterministic evals on seeded prompts and compute token-level divergence and perplexity delta; use a rolling statistical window and non-parametric test to avoid false positives when sample sizes are small. Telemetry surfaces per-tenant resume progress, shard checksums, snapshot lag, and node bootstrap time.

Terraform/IaC integration: Provide two Terraform modules and a small hook script: (a) operator_module: installs the operator into the private control-plane namespace and configures object-store credentials + snapshot lifecycle policy; (b) traffic_enforcer_module: deploys a short-lived eBPF-based traffic fence that can split traffic at the VPC ENI level for ramping. The operator exposes a plan step that can be run from CI: terraform plan shows operator intent and will attach a preflight job to validate snapshot write permissions and cross-account role access.

Safety and tradeoffs: Lockless leases increase parallel upgrade velocity but require careful lease granularity to avoid conflicting writes; we default to tenant-slice level. Snapshotting to object store adds S3 egress/storage cost and must be lifecycle-managed; snapshots are incremental and deduplicated by content-hash to minimize cost. Resume semantics demand strict checksum verification and idempotent replays. Complex correctness checks increase upgrade latency for the first rollout; to mitigate we allow a fast-path for low-risk minor patch upgrades that skip costly correctness tests under a guardrail flag.

Acceptance criteria (start):
- Operator can complete a staged upgrade across a 10-slice test VPC with zero customer-visible errors and tail-latency within SLO.
- Resume test: simulate failure after 35% of nodes upgraded; operator resumes and finishes upgrade without manual intervention.
- Rollback test: introduce a deterministic regression (model mismatch) post-upgrade; operator can rollback to previous release in <5 minutes for the test slice while meeting health gates.

Deliverables: Terraform modules, operator helm chart, e2e harness (kitchen tests), PRD section for customer-facing runbook, runbook GH issue template, and a short RFC for the S3 snapshot schema.

Open questions:
- Default snapshot retention policy and expected cost allocation for BYO object store customers.
- Tenant slice size heuristics for lease granularity (latency vs. parallelism tradeoff).
- Whether to support HSM-backed snapshot signatures for high-security customers (affects performance).

Links: design doc (confluence): https://redwood.company/confluence/private/lockless-snapshot-resume, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13820, terraform example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/tree/main/operator-lockless
comments: 2025-02-11: Triage meeting notes: agreed to pursue lockless approach; Marco to prototype snapshot shard format. Action: Aisha to draft operator RBAC requirements.

2025-02-18: Design review (Eng + Security + PM). Security requested HSM signature option and encrypted snapshot metadata. Marked as security_review_required. Decision: implement optional signing in v1.1.

2025-02-22: Prototype PR opened (runtime#13820). Prototype shows resumable download/upload of snapshot shards with checksumming. Initial perf: 250ms median shard-apply time for 10k-entry shard on c5.large-like VM.

2025-02-26: Integration spike with Terraform modules completed. operator_module exposes preflight job; traffic_enforcer_module uses eBPF shim. Running terraform plan against staging VPC succeeded but blocked in CI due to missing cross-account role. Created dependency ENG-412356 to address cross-account role automation.

2025-02-28: e2e harness job failed intermittently in network-constrained environment. Root cause: object-store accelerated endpoints were not available in test VPC; added fallback to chunked retry and exponential backoff. Next: validate resume under packet loss.
2025-03-01: Running formal acceptance tests next week. Schedule: run acceptance on 2025-03-09, then security review on 2025-03-12.
